description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).

Hand-built 3-layer circuit without LayerNorm: copy query digit via prev-pos attention, uniform-attention digit histogram (masked to positions 0-9), ReLU gating to select n_q, position-gated step decoding into tens/units digits.

Knob version of the circuit, 3 layers, d_model 80: copy query digit by attention to position 10, uniform-attention digit histogram over positions 0-9, ReLU gating to select n_q, position-gated decoding into tens/units digits. LayerNorm removed.

2 layers: copy query digit by attention to position 10; uniform-attention digit histogram over positions 0-9 with ReLU selection of n_q, position gating folded into layer 2's MLP; linear readout head.
Same 2-layer circuit as TwoLayerGated with the MLP width cut to the 220 hidden units it needs (d_ff 256 -> 220).
Same 2-layer circuit with 2 attention heads instead of 4 (head width 40): head 0 copies the query, head 1 builds the digit histogram.
2-layer circuit with the digit-selection gating margin shrunk from 100 to 20 (K=2, counts <= 10). Works at 20; later runs show G=15 also works and G=10 leaks.
2-layer circuit with threshold steepness K=1 (ramp slope 1 instead of 2). Ablation: a unit-slope ramp gives only 0.5 at n = t, so the indicators are ambiguous.
2-layer circuit with residual width cut from 80 to 68: the 2-layer design never uses the unused L/X slots, so the width only needs to cover up to ST_10 (dim 67).

Ablation of TwoLayerDmodel68: remove the position gating of the threshold indicators and the readout (POS_GATE=False). The selection then fires at every output position, so the tens and units digits are mixed.

2-layer circuit with query-match attention in the histogram head: keys match the digit token, with score weight log(2) so each matching digit counts 2x against non-matches; the histogram is then a normalized fraction (theta shifted accordingly).
Ablation of TwoLayerDmodel68: remove the key mask on positions 10-12 (BIG=0) from the histogram head. The uniform average then includes the query and separator tokens, so the counts are diluted.
Sensitivity test of TwoLayerDmodel68 with copy-attention strength ALPHA 30 -> 3. Tests whether the copy head needs a sharp query selector.
Sensitivity test of TwoLayerDmodel68 with copy-attention strength ALPHA 30 -> 10: find where the copy head stops working.
Sensitivity test of TwoLayerDmodel68 with threshold steepness K 2 -> 4 (sharper ramp, same thresholds).
3-layer variant with the position gate removed from the layer-3 readout (POS_GATE=False). Ablation: tens and units logits both fire, so the output digits are mixed.
3-layer variant with scalar count decoding: layer 2 writes n_q into a scalar X via a ReLU layer, layer 3 decodes [X == c] with a second-difference bump (3 ReLUs per digit, position-gated).
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with a weaker key mask on positions 10-12 (BIG 50 -> 20): the mask only has to beat the 0 logit of the digit positions.
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with gating margin G 20 -> 10, checking how small the margin can get before non-query bins leak through.
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with gating margin G 20 -> 5 (second point on the margin curve).
2-layer circuit with threshold steepness K=3 and gating margin G=20 (both knobs in the working range).
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with copy-attention strength ALPHA 10 -> 1 (lower bound of the working range).
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with copy-attention strength ALPHA 5, locating the threshold between the failing (3) and working (10) settings.
Reproduction of the chosen 2-layer configuration (D68, 4 heads, ALPHA 30, BIG 20, K 3, G 20) as a final check after the sensitivity sweep.
2-layer circuit with 2 attention heads at width 68 (head dim 34) instead of 4 heads: head 0 copies the query, head 1 builds the digit histogram.
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with a weak key mask (BIG 20 -> 5) to find where the mask stops mattering.
Sensitivity test of the 2-layer circuit with a large gating margin (G 20 -> 50). The margin only needs to be big enough to suppress non-query bins, so large values should still work.
3-layer version with threshold-step decoding (the Knobs3L80 design, with K 3 and G 20): copy, histogram+select, then position-gated step readout into tens/units logits.
Sensitivity test of the chosen 2-layer configuration with gating margin G 20 -> 15, to locate the lower edge of the margin range (G 10 gave 0.94).
Ablation of the 3-layer step circuit with the key mask removed (BIG=0), to compare with the 2-layer NoMask ablation (0.585).
3-layer bump-decoding circuit at the chosen copy strength (ALPHA 30, BIG 50, G 20), as a final variant of the bump decoder.
